facts.text: The 1952 UFO flap sparked a nationwide media frenzy, with Washington, D.C. at its epicenter as reporters chased sightings over the capital.
During the summer of 1952, Air Force radar stations in Washington, D.C. logged over 700 new UFO reports, a dramatic jump from the 615 recorded in the previous four years.
UFO historian Curtis Peebles described the 1952 incident as the “climax of the UFO flap,” noting it was the most publicized sighting ever linked to the nation's capital.
On two consecutive Saturday nights in July 1952, unidentified objects hovered 15 miles south‑southwest of Washington, D.C., without following any known flight paths.
Life magazine’s April 7, 1952 issue, featuring Marilyn Monroe, ran a headline “Have We Visitors From Space?” that helped turn the UFO debate into a mainstream conversation.
The Washington, D.C. UFO incident remains a key chapter in the city’s history, illustrating how a sudden wave of unexplained sightings can capture national attention.
